number of books read over the summer by the students in two different English classes. What is the positive difference between the ranges of number of books read over the summer for the two classes?\x3C/p>",rationale:"\x3Cp style=\"text-align: left;\">The correct answer is \x3Cmath alttext=\"4\">\x3Cmn>4\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. It's given that the two boxplots show the distribution of number of books read over the summer by the students in two different English classes. In a boxplot, the first vertical line represents the minimum value of the data set and the last vertical line represents the maximum value of the data set. The range of a data set is the difference between its maximum value and its minimum value. In class A, the maximum number of books read is \x3Cmath alttext=\"5\">\x3Cmn>5\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> and the minimum number of books read is \x3Cmath alttext=\"0\">\x3Cmn>0\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. The difference between those values is \x3Cmath alttext=\"5 minus 0\">\x3Cmn>5\x3C/mn>\x3Cmo>-\x3C/mo>\x3Cmn>0\x3C/mn>\x3C/math>, or \x3Cmath alttext=\"5\">\x3Cmn>5\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. Therefore, the range of the number of books read in class A is \x3Cmath alttext=\"5\">\x3Cmn>5\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. In class B, the maximum number of books read is \x3Cmath alttext=\"10\">\x3Cmn>10\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> and the minimum number of books read is \x3Cmath alttext=\"1\">\x3Cmn>1\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. The difference between those values is \x3Cmath alttext=\"10 minus 1\">\x3Cmn>10\x3C/mn>\x3Cmo>-\x3C/mo>\x3Cmn>1\x3C/mn>\x3C/math>, or \x3Cmath alttext=\"9\">\x3Cmn>9\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. Therefore, the range of the number of books read in class B is \x3Cmath alttext=\"9\">\x3Cmn>9\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. To find the positive difference between the ranges of the number of books read for the two classes, the smaller range must be subtracted from the larger range. Therefore, the positive difference between the ranges of number of books read over the summer for the two classes is \x3Cmath alttext=\"9 minus 5\">\x3Cmn>9\x3C/mn>\x3Cmo>-\x3C/mo>\x3Cmn>5\x3C/mn>\x3C/math>, or \x3Cmath alttext=\"4\">\x3Cmn>4\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>.\x3C/p>"},answers:$R[4]=[$R[5]={id:14103,question:935369962,correct:!0,content:"4"}],userData:void 0})($R["server-fn:0"]))
